metadataReview.note: Reviewed approximate hill-sector location: the Haus der Bayerischen Geschichte identifies the 15 October 1805 assault on the Michaelsberg heights overlooking Ulm; the French defence catalogue independently names Michelsberg. The atlas point represents the summit sector of that hill. The later Wilhelmsburg provides a modern geographical reference because Ulm/Neu-Ulm Touristik explicitly places it on the hilltop. The fortress dates from 1842–1849 and is not identified as an 1805 fortification or the exact site of a combat action. Only hill-sector precision is claimed; the battlefield perimeter and troop positions remain unknown.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: Approximate summit-sector marker, not a surveyed battlefield point. The official tourism page places the modern Wilhelmsburg on the Michelsberg hilltop and publishes locationDetail.center as {lat:48.4112119,lng:9.9830469}. Convert to atlas [longitude,latitude] order and round to three decimals: [9.983,48.411]. The rounding describes numerical display resolution only; it does not establish 100-metre historical accuracy. Geographic scope is the named hill sector. No measured uncertainty radius or exact combat footprint is established; the post-1805 building is used solely to locate the surviving landform.
